lines.text:
My English Classroom

Our English classroom is on the second floor of the school building. It is a bright, spacious room with large windows that let in plenty of natural light.

At the front of the room, there is a whiteboard where the teacher writes vocabulary and grammar rules. Next to it, there is a projector screen that the teacher uses for presentations and videos. The teacher's desk sits in the corner with a laptop, a stack of textbooks, and a cup of pens and markers.

The students sit at individual desks arranged in rows. Each desk has a drawer for storing notebooks, pencils, and erasers. Some students keep a pencil case with highlighters, a ruler, and a sharpener. There is a bookshelf at the back of the room filled with dictionaries, readers, and reference books.

On the walls, there are posters with grammar charts, a world map, and a bulletin board where the teacher pins student work and important notices. A clock on the wall helps everyone keep track of time during lessons.

The classroom also has a cupboard where supplies are kept: paper, scissors, glue, tape, and folders. Near the door, there is a recycling bin and a regular bin for rubbish.

During lessons, the teacher often asks us to work in pairs or groups. We move our chairs together and discuss topics, complete worksheets, or practise dialogues. I enjoy our classroom — it is where I started to feel confident speaking English.

lines.text: 'Homework' = work done at home. 'Coursework' = ongoing assessed work during a course. 'Assignment' = a specific task given by the teacher. All three are uncountable or used with 'an/a piece of'.
